title: AI-Assisted Software Development
description: Learn to use AI coding assistants, IDE copilots, and agentic coding tools as professional software-development tools while preserving developer understanding, verification, security, and ownership of the resulting code.

nodes.label: AI Tool Mental Model
nodes.description: Adopt the mental model that AI assistants propose while the developer defines goals, evaluates tradeoffs, and owns the result, and recognize AI's genuine strengths (boilerplate, explanation, search) alongside its weaknesses (hallucinated APIs, overconfidence).

nodes.label: AI Tool Categories
nodes.description: Distinguish chat assistants, IDE-integrated copilots, and CLI/agentic coding tools, and choose the right one deliberately based on task size and risk — from a syntax question to a high-risk production change.

nodes.label: Prompt Construction
nodes.description: Write task prompts that state the goal, relevant context, constraints, non-goals, and a clear definition of done, and ask the assistant to investigate before proposing a large change to an uncertain problem.

nodes.label: Context Engineering
nodes.description: Treat context as a limited resource — supplying relevant files, tests, and error output progressively rather than dumping a whole repository — and keep context hygienic by correcting stale assumptions and starting fresh when a conversation becomes misleading.

nodes.label: Repository Exploration
nodes.description: Learn an unfamiliar repository before changing it by following entry points, structure, and tests, and use AI-assisted search and questioning to build an accurate local mental model rather than guessing.

nodes.label: Task Decomposition
nodes.description: Break large work into small, independently verifiable units, separate planning from execution with an explicit review step, and keep diffs small enough to understand, test, and revert.

nodes.label: Explanation & Learning
nodes.description: Use AI as a tutor to explain unfamiliar code and translate terse documentation, while avoiding passive copying by explaining, predicting, and reproducing important patterns yourself.

nodes.label: Code Generation & Refactoring
nodes.description: Generate bounded, well-scoped code that fits existing naming and architecture conventions, and use AI to refactor safely — establishing tests as a baseline first and requiring a diff-level explanation of behavioral impact.

nodes.label: Debugging & Testing with AI
nodes.description: Supply reproducible evidence (errors, stack traces, recent changes) for hypothesis-driven AI-assisted debugging instead of shotgun-fixing, and treat AI-generated tests with the same scrutiny as production code since they can assert the implementation instead of the requirement.

nodes.label: Verification & Git Safety
nodes.description: Climb a verification ladder from reading the diff through compiling, testing, and manual checks proportional to a change's impact, and use Git status/diff/commit as a safety boundary that makes AI-driven changes easy to inspect and revert.

nodes.label: Agentic Coding
nodes.description: Understand the inspect-plan-edit-run-observe agent loop, grant only the permission level a task actually needs, and define explicit stop conditions for destructive, ambiguous, or high-risk decisions.

nodes.description: Recognize common coding hallucinations such as nonexistent methods or invented flags and demand evidence for claims, and apply security discipline — protecting secrets, treating repository content as untrusted, and scrutinizing destructive actions and suggested dependencies.
